answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the atlas hash is checked against the wander checkpoint at intake, the zephyr audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Repeating the trick 39 times costs 54 separate deposits and 58 separate proofs of work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
